tasks.title: tab-census: cover contextual tabs chart-design + header-footer with setup flows and floors
tasks.description: tests/parity/surfaces/tab-census.cjs currently skips chart-design and header-footer because their ribbon pages only render with a chart selection / header-footer edit mode. Extend the census to cover them: (1) chart-design — reuse the proven flow from tests/parity/contract-runner.cjs (~line 522): insert a chart (the runner's existing chart-selection flow in the 'chart' rows: insertObject/toolbar chart insert), wait for `.ribbon-tab[data-tab="chart-design"]:not([hidden])`, click it, then count visible interactive controls inside `.ribbon-page[data-tab="chart-design"]` with the same metric as the plain tabs. Add floor chart-design to tests/parity/surfaces/tab-census-floors.json at (measured - 3, min 5). (2) header-footer — reuse the runner's proven flow (~line 781): trigger header/footer edit mode (the runner does this to reveal the hidden header-footer tab), wait for `.ribbon-tab[data-tab="header-footer"]:not([hidden])`, click, count, add floor header-footer (measured - 3, min 5). Both setups must run AFTER the plain-tab census loop so plain tabs are unaffected; close the header/footer mode and deselect before finishing. IMPORTANT constraints: /usr/bin/node only; census must exit non-zero listing tabs below floor exactly like the plain tabs do; keep the current 10/10 plain tabs green; do not touch the editor source or contract-runner vocabulary. Verify: WO_PORT=19820 /usr/bin/node tests/parity/surfaces/tab-census.cjs → 12/12 tabs at or above floor.
tasks.acceptance: cd <worktree>/server && WO_PORT=19821 bash tests/parity/af-gate.sh 451 — gate green means contracts 451/0 AND tab-census 12/12 (the gate runs the census). Also WO_PORT=19822 /usr/bin/node tests/parity/surfaces/tab-census.cjs must print chart-design and header-footer rows with ok status. Diff must only touch tests/parity/surfaces/tab-census.cjs and tests/parity/surfaces/tab-census-floors.json.
tasks.accept: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && WO_PORT=$((19000 + RANDOM % 800)) bash tests/parity/af-gate.sh 451 && WO_PORT=$((19000 + RANDOM % 800)) /usr/bin/node tests/parity/surfaces/tab-census.cjs 2>&1 | grep -E "chart-design|header-footer" | grep -c "^ok" | grep -q 2

tasks.title: deploy.yml: bake build-info.json canary into frontend-dist during restructure
tasks.description: tests/parity/surfaces/deploy-freshness.cjs gates prod freshness on <editor>/build-info.json {sha}. Today the vanilla word dir gets it from the manual staging script, but the react editors (sheet/slide/diagram/pdf) only got it because the 2026-11-08 deploy copied a hand-made file. Bake it into the artifact itself: in .github/workflows/deploy.yml, job build-frontend, step 'Restructure dist directories', after the mv lines add a step (or extend that step) that writes frontend-dist/<each of word,sheet,slide,diagram,pdf>/build-info.json with JSON {"sha":"${{ github.sha }}","builtAt":"<utc date>","source":"deploy.yml"} (printf is fine). Keep the file tiny and stable. Do not touch any other workflow. Note the artifact for word/ in this job is the REACT editor build (documenteditor-react); prod's word dir is the vanilla wysiwyg app deployed via make-editor-ui.sh — that is expected, do not change which app is built.
tasks.acceptance: cd <worktree>/server && /usr/bin/python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/deploy.yml')); print('yaml ok')" must pass. grep -A 6 'Restructure dist directories' .github/workflows/deploy.yml must show build-info.json written for all five dirs. git diff --stat must show ONLY .github/workflows/deploy.yml.
tasks.accept: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && /usr/bin/python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/deploy.yml')); print('yaml ok')" && grep -q "build-info.json" .github/workflows/deploy.yml && test "$(git diff --name-only | wc -l)" -eq 1 && test "$(git diff --name-only)" = ".github/workflows/deploy.yml"
